analysis.investment_thesis: Affle is one of India's finest digital advertising technology businesses — 45%+ revenue and profit CAGR over 7 years, virtually debt-free, strong free cash flow — but at INR 20,649 Cr and P/E of 47x, this is a ship that sailed for SMILE investors years ago. Excellent business, wrong entry point.
key_strengths: Exceptional compounding machine: revenue grew from INR 167 Cr (FY18) to INR 2,266 Cr (FY25) at 45.1% CAGR while maintaining free cash flow (INR 266 Cr in FY25, up from INR 41 Cr in FY20)
Near-zero debt (D/E 0.01), INR 1,047 Cr cash on balance sheet, and OCF positive for 5 consecutive years — pristine financial health
Promoter at 54.92% with global platform acquisitions (Mediasmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi) building a genuine programmatic mobile ad ecosystem with switching costs
key_risks: At P/E 47x on INR 20,649 Cr market cap, even 25% annual growth for 3 years barely justifies the current price — no margin of safety
ROE of 14% understates returns (goodwill from acquisitions inflates equity base), but integration risk across 5 acquired platforms remains real
Digital advertising is cyclical and vulnerable to macro slowdowns, privacy regulation changes (app tracking transparency), and platform risk from Google/Meta
red_flags: Market cap INR 20,649 Cr — this is a mid-to-large cap; FII at 16.66% and DII at 17.90% mean it is thoroughly discovered
Operating margin at 18.1% is declining relative to the scale expected for a tech platform — gross margin of 29% is thin for a software business
Capex is accelerating (INR 160 Cr in FY25 vs INR 73 Cr in FY22) — the supposedly asset-light model is getting heavier
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Affle is the kind of company I would have loved to own at INR 500-2,000 Cr market cap — a technology-driven, asset-light business riding India's digital advertising boom with promoter conviction. The numbers over 7 years are outstanding: 45% revenue CAGR, consistent OCF generation, and debt-free balance sheet. The global acquisition strategy has created a meaningful programmatic advertising ecosystem covering app discovery, retargeting, and omnichannel DSPs.

But at INR 20,649 Cr and 47x earnings, the boat has left the dock for a SMILE investor. The market has fully priced the growth story. ROE at 14% is only adequate, and the thin gross margins (29%) for what is positioned as a tech platform raise questions about true pricing power versus pass-through ad spend. Worth watching if the stock corrects 40-50% to bring the P/E to 25-28x — that would make it interesting again. As it stands, existing holders should hold; new investors should wait.
